newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US construction activity seen up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US construction activity seen up in 1997.

text.p: Total U.S. construction activity is expected to rise 4.0 percent to $333.6 billion in 1997, the sixth straight rise since the 1991 recession, according to a McGraw-Hill forecast.

Increased construction of offices, hotels, multi-family housing and new schools is expected to lead the growth, McGraw-Hill's Construction Information Group said in releasing the outlook at its annual conference of industry executives.
The group said it expects moderate growth in construction next year despite predictions for slower overall economic growth of about 2.0 percent.

Overall institutional building is expected to rise 5.0 percent to 422 million square feet in 1997, according to the McGraw-Hill outlook. Manufacturing construction is forecast to bounce back 4.0 percent to 144 million square feet.
Income property square footage is expected to rise 5.0 percent, with office construction leading the sector with a 12.0 percent gain over the year before, the forecast said.
The group said it expects construction of single-family housing to decline modestly in 1997, with dwelling units down 4.0 percent to 1.035 million units and dollar volume slipping 1.0 percent.
